inputs.original_text: Five months have passed since the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, yet airstrikes are continuing to slaughter civilians and the humanitarian crisis facing Palestinians is still incredibly dire. This isn't some short-term consequence—it's a calculated dismantling of these communities' links to their pre-war existence, driving them into a harsher, more violent life under relentless attack. The powerful forces are once again demonstrating the grip of structural inequality and historical oppression that keep vulnerable populations locked in cycles of violence and dispossession. 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, put it this way: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” What we really need is institutional reform to protect the oppressed and put an end to these injustices.
inputs.modified_text: It's been five months since the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, but airstrikes are still slaughtering civilians and the humanitarian crisis for Palestinians remains devastatingly dire. This isn't a temporary fallout—it's a deliberate effort to strip these communities of their pre-war lives and trap them in harsher, more violent conditions under constant assault. Powerful interests are once again revealing how structural inequality and deep-rooted historical oppression lock vulnerable populations into cycles of violence and dispossession. As 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five displaced in Deir al-Balah, described it: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” We urgently need institutional reform to defend the oppressed and dismantle these injustices for good.
